entry.literal: horsemen / horses; and he brought evil; the help of the workers of iniquity; he growls; the fullness of shepherds; he does not bow down; to wage war on/against Mount Zion; like birds flying; shielding and rescuing, passing over and delivering; turn to the one against whom they made the revolt deep, children of Israel; they will reject; sin (adverbial); and he will flee for himself; for forced labor; and his rock will pass away from terror; fire; furnace / oven
entry.standardEnglish: ASV throughout; alternatives from JPS 1917 and NJPS 1985 (checked on Sefaria 2026-11-26) recorded in commentary
entry.wohChoice: 31:1 pārāšîm 'horsemen' (ASV, JPS 1917; as at 21:7; 22:6-7). 31:2 wayyāḇēʾ rāʿ 'and will bring evil' (ASV future; JPS 1917 present and NJPS past in commentary); rāʿ 'evil', not the 45:7 'calamity'; ʿezraṯ 'the help' (NJPS 'allies' in commentary). 31:4 liṣbōʾ ʿal-har-ṣiyyôn 'to fight upon Mount Zion and upon its hill' (ASV, JPS 1917), keeping the spatial sense of ʿal and leaving open the hostile reading of NJPS 'make war against' and of the stable 29:7-8 'fight against'; yehgeh 'growls'; mᵉlōʾ rōʿîm 'a multitude of shepherds'; lōʾ yaʿăneh 'nor does he abase himself'. 31:5 'Like birds hovering'; 'he will protect and deliver it, he will pass over and preserve it' (ASV, 'it' supplied); the Passover echo of psḥ (Exod 12:13, 23, 27) in commentary only. 31:6 'Turn, O children of Israel, to him from whom they have deeply revolted': MT's third person kept with NJPS, vocative moved forward (changed from the draft's ASV harmonisation 'you have deeply revolted'). 31:7 yimʾāsûn 'shall reject' (NJPS; concordant with 5:24 'rejected'; changed from the draft's 'cast away', which the book keeps for hišlîḵ at 2:20); ḥēṭʾ 'as a sin'. 31:8 'Assyria … him' (as 10:5, 24); wᵉnās lô 'he shall flee' (nws; NJPS nss 'shrivel' in commentary); lāmas 'forced labor'. 31:9 'his rock shall pass away by reason of terror' (ASV, JPS 1917; changed from the draft's 'for terror'); ʾûr 'fire'; tannûr 'furnace'.
entry.rationale: Each item is a site where the Hebrew is ambiguous or rare. The line keeps a standard public-domain rendering, usually ASV and often shared by JPS 1917, and the commentary reports the alternatives; three items change the Translator's draft. (a) 31:4 is the main crux. The verb ṣbʾ with ʿal means 'wage war against' (29:7-8, the same phrase ʿal-har ṣiyyôn; Num 31:7; Zech 14:12), and NJPS reads 'will descend to make war / Against the mount and the hill of Zion', so that the lion is YHWH and Zion his prey. ASV and JPS 1917 read 'to fight upon mount Zion', which allows a defensive battle and agrees with the protection of v. 5; the same verse uses ʿal spatially ('over his prey'). The line keeps 'upon', the basic spatial sense of the preposition, because it renders the Hebrew without settling a question the commentators still debate; 'against' would settle it one way and 'for' the other, and 'for' has no lexical support. The concordance with 29:8 is stated in the commentary. (b) 31:6 shifts from an imperative to a third-person verb. ASV and JPS 1917 bring the clause into the second person; NJPS keeps the third person with a vocative (checked). The line follows NJPS, because the change of person is MT's and an English reader can follow it once the vocative stands first; the subject analysis of bᵉnê yiśrāʾēl and NJPS's recorded emendation are reported. (c) 31:7 yimʾāsûn is from mʾs 'reject' (BDB; HALOT), which the book prints as 'rejected' at 5:24 and NJPS renders 'reject' here. ASV's 'cast away' copies 2:20, where the verb is hišlîḵ 'throw', so the draft gave two verbs one English word. (d) 31:9 'by reason of terror' restores the ASV and JPS 1917 wording for causal min; the draft's 'for terror' could be read as purpose. The remaining items follow ASV: pārāšîm 'horsemen' is the book's established gloss, although the noun can denote horses (HALOT, recalled); the future 'will bring evil' reads the wayyiqtol with the following weqatal; rāʿ is 'evil' with ASV and JPS 1917, and the 45:7 'calamity' entry is not extended because its rationale rests on the merism with šālôm. At 31:5 psḥ is the verb of Exod 12:13, 23, 27; 'pass over' is the ASV and JPS 1917 rendering, and the Passover echo is kept to commentary. At 31:8 NJPS derives wᵉnās from nss and lāmas from mss ('shrivel', 'pine away'); the line keeps the usual nws 'flee' and mas 'forced labor'. 'Forced labor' is the modern English for the corvée that ASV calls 'taskwork'; the central mas-oved entry keeps 'taskwork' for the compound at Gen 49:15, and that cross-corpus difference is flagged in the editor report. The entry is direct, because every rendering is attested in ASV, JPS 1917 or NJPS, except 31:8 lāmas 'forced labor' and 31:1 'lean on', which give the standard lexical sense (BDB, HALOT) of the noun and verb; no reading is added.

rationaleAppend: Wave I-5 (Isa 31): 'Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help' at 31:1, hôy before a participle as at 29:15 (ASV and JPS 1917 'Woe to them that go down'; NJPS 'Ha!'; checked 2026-11-26).

Wave I-5 (Isa 31): the Translator's descriptive title 'Isaiah 31 — Woe to those who go down to Egypt: YHWH like a lion and like hovering birds over Jerusalem' is kept. Divine speech after 'thus YHWH has said to me' (31:4) is not in quotation marks; nᵉʾum-YHWH is 'says YHWH' (31:9), as at 14:22 and 17:6.
Wave I-5 (Isa 31): 'YHWH of hosts' at 31:4 (with the cognate infinitive liṣbōʾ 'to fight', the same word-play as 13:4) and 31:5.

Wave I-5 (Isa 31): three applications. At 31:3 ʾāḏām is the predicate of kind in the antithesis ʾāḏām wᵉlōʾ-ʾēl and is rendered by the adjective, 'the Egyptians are human, and not God' (NJPS 'are man'; ASV and JPS 1917 'are men'); 'humankind' would not fit a predicate. At 31:7 the distributive ʾîš with singular suffixes is 'everyone … their idols', the pronoun rule of 2:20 (ASV and JPS 1917 'every man his'; NJPS 'everyone … his'). At 31:8 the refrain pair is negated, bᵉḥereḇ lōʾ-ʾîš wᵉḥereḇ lōʾ-ʾāḏām 'by a sword not of a human, and a sword not of humankind' (NJPS 'not by the sword of man; a sword not of humans'): both nouns are generic, a sword wielded by no human being, so wave I-4 rule 13 ('men' for specific male groups) does not apply.

Wave I-5 (Isa 31): at 31:3 ʾēl in the antithesis ʾāḏām wᵉlōʾ-ʾēl names the divine category set against the human one, the term the denial rules out, and is rendered 'God' with ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS (checked 2026-11-26). The indefinite 'a god' was considered and not adopted: the verse contrasts orders of being, not Egypt with a particular deity.

Wave I-5 (Isa 31): a third context. At 31:3 bāśār wᵉlōʾ-rûaḥ sets rûaḥ against bāśār as the divine order of being against the creaturely, in parallel with ʾāḏām wᵉlōʾ-ʾēl in the first colon. The rendering is lower-case 'spirit', with ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS ('flesh, not spirit'; checked 2026-11-26). 'Breath' (the 40:7 context clause) was considered and not adopted, because horses have breath and the colon does not contrast breathing with not breathing. The rûaḥ here is not an endowment or outpouring, so the site extends the entry's scope; the wohChoice wording is unchanged.

Wave I-5 (Isa 31): 'his princes shall be dismayed at the signal' at 31:9, one of the expected banner sites named in wohChoice. ASV and JPS 1917 have 'at the ensign'; NJPS derives minnēs from nss and reads 'shall collapse from weakness', noting 'meaning of Heb. uncertain' (checked 2026-11-26). The derivation from nēs is kept and the NJPS reading is reported in commentary.
